stem: The starting annual salary for an office worker at a company is $29,000. If the company awards an annual increase of 6.2%, which graph models this situation after the office worker receives x annual increases?

options.label: A
options.text: [Graph A: Linear graph starting at 29,000 and increasing steadily]

options.label: B
options.text: [Graph B: Steep curve sharply increasing near y-axis and exceeding 50,000 quickly]

options.label: C
options.text: [Graph C: Exponential curve starting near 5,000 rapidly rising, not matching start]

options.label: D
options.text: [Graph D: Gradual upward curve starting below 10,000 and curving upwards]

visual_elements: Graph A: Line graph labeled 'Office Worker's Salary' with y-axis Annual Salary (dollars) from 0 to 50,000 and x-axis Number of Annual Increases from 0 to 10. Line starts near 29,000 and increases linearly.
Graph B: Steep exponential or sharper curve rising very quickly exceeding 50,000 quickly, starting near zero or below starting salary.
Graph C: Exponential curve starting near around 5,000, increasing rapidly but does not start at 29,000.
Graph D: Exponential growth curve rising gradually from below 10,000 towards 35,000 at 10 increases.
notes: The problem involves exponential growth due to percentage increase; thus, Graph A (linear) and Graphs B and C with improper starts can be ruled out. Graph D matches an exponential growth curve starting near the given salary and rising gradually.
